steps.text: Part 3 of 4: Mate with king and queen: the supported check. This part covers Near misses. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

steps.title: Same queen move, the king one step away
steps.prompt: White plays the same queen move in both positions. In the second the white king is on e6 instead of f7. Predict the result each time, then check.

steps.title: Distance mate, and the king one file out
steps.prompt: Predict first. In the second position the white king stands one file further from the black king. In the third the black king is in a corner.

steps.title: Mate, and the stalemate next to it
steps.prompt: Predict first. The second position moves both the white king and the queen from the first; say which change matters. In the third the colours are reversed.

steps.title: Can White mate at once?
steps.prompt: Predict first. In the second position the white king is one rank further away, on b5. In the third the black king sits on g8.
Each near miss changed one small thing, and the result changed completely. Pick the near miss you found hardest and say what changed.

fields.label: The small change, and what it did:

steps.text: **Remember.** One small change can turn mate into a draw or a slower win: a king one step away, or one rank further. So never trust a move just because it worked before. Check where both kings stand, then ask the three questions again: can the king take her, is a square free, can Black still move? A move that fails any of them is not mate.
